_comment: Single source of truth for release notes. The What's New window reads the entry matching the running version, and scripts/release.ps1 reads the same entry for the GitHub release body. Keep both fed by adding one entry per release BEFORE running release.ps1 — the script refuses to release a version with no entry here, which is what stops the notes silently going stale the way the old hardcoded heredoc did.

welcome.title: Welcome to TakeOff
welcome.subtitle: Open everything you need, exactly where you want it, in one click.

sections.heading: Getting started
items: Click the + on the launcher bar to make your first group.
Add apps, files, folders, websites and Steam games to it.
Click the group to launch everything in it at once.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
items: Every item can open on a specific monitor and virtual desktop — set it with the Desktop and Screen dropdowns, or drag windows where you want them with Edit Layout.
Items launch top to bottom; drag them to change the order.
Right-click the launcher bar for settings, or press Ctrl+Alt+Space to summon it from anywhere.

sections.heading: Faster at startup
items: TakeOff now starts right as your desktop appears, instead of up to a minute later. Startup groups launch sooner too.
Nothing to set up — it switches over the first time this version runs.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Uninstalling TakeOff now fully removes it from startup.
The installer now closes a running TakeOff before updating it.

sections.heading: Anonymous usage data — please read
items: TakeOff now sends a short weekly message so I can see how many people use it and which features are worth building on. This is on by default.
It contains only numbers: how many groups and items you have, which item types, your TakeOff and Windows versions, and whether you have a license.
It never includes your group names, file paths, web addresses, or which apps you launch. Counts, never content.
See exactly what it sends, from your own installation, in Settings → Privacy. Turn it off there too — it stops immediately.

sections.heading: Faster startup
items: TakeOff now appears almost immediately after you log in, instead of up to a minute later. Windows was holding it back; it now starts a different way.

sections.heading: Capture Current
items: Build a group from the windows you already have open. Arrange things how you like them, then press Capture Current in the group editor.
It records each window's monitor, position, size and virtual desktop — so launching the group puts everything back exactly where it was.
You get a preview first, with everything ticked, so you can leave out anything you don't want.
Windows you've already added are flagged, so capturing twice won't duplicate them.
Browser tabs aren't included — add those with the bookmark picker as usual.

sections.heading: What's New
items: This window. After an update, TakeOff shows you what changed.
Click the version number at the bottom of Settings to read it again any time.

sections.heading: Launch groups when Windows starts
items: Any group can now open automatically when Windows starts. Turn it on in the group editor, or right-click a group on the launcher bar.
Groups launch one at a time, in the order they appear on the bar — drag them to change it.
Hold Shift while Windows is starting to skip the launch entirely.
Requires a license.

sections.heading: Improvements
items: Left-click the TakeOff icon in the system tray to bring the launcher bar back into view.
The group editor and settings windows no longer stay on top of everything else, so clicking another window now brings it forward properly.
Bigger, clearer icons and text throughout the item and app lists.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Fixed launching items onto specific virtual desktops on Windows 10, which previously opened them on whichever desktop you were already on.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Windows apps now show their real icons instead of a generic placeholder.
Steam games show their icons again.
Feedback now reaches us with the details we need to actually reproduce a problem — and you can include your setup and an email address if you'd like a reply.
